definitions.explanation: Having vivid, bright, and striking colors. Used to describe things that are visually impressive due to their rich coloring.

examples.japanese: {色鮮|いろあざ}やかな{花|はな}が{咲|さ}いている。
{色鮮|いろあざ}やかな{着物|きもの}を{着|き}た{女性|じょせい}が{目|め}を{引|ひ}いた。
examples.english: A woman wearing a brightly colored kimono caught my eye.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると{山|やま}は{色鮮|いろあざ}やかな{紅葉|こうよう}に{染|そ}まり、{多|おお}くの{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{訪|おとず}れる。
examples.english: In autumn, the mountains are dyed with vivid fall colors, attracting many tourists.

notes:
USAGE:
{色鮮|いろあざ}やか is a compound of {色|いろ} (color) and {鮮|あざ}やか (vivid). It functions as a na-adjective, used with な before nouns and に before verbs.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {色鮮|いろあざ}やかな{花|はな} (colorful flowers)
- {色鮮|いろあざ}やかな{料理|りょうり} (colorful dishes)
- {色鮮|いろあざ}やかな{紅葉|こうよう} (vivid autumn leaves)
- {色鮮|いろあざ}やかに{彩|いろど}る (to color vividly)

SIMILAR WORDS:
カラフル (colorful) is a casual loanword alternative. {鮮|あざ}やか alone means "vivid" but can refer to skill or technique, not just color.
